VENs in the UDERMS network must communicate with VOLTTRON agents as well as OCPP servers. To enable this, the project team worked together to ensure that the project’s push-mode implementation of OpenADR interfaces smoothly with the USU EMS and OCPP servers. Given these successful tests, the custom VEN module was to be implemented in VOLTTRON agents across the system in Budget Period 3. The figure below depicts how an OpenADR VEN interacts with a VOLTTRON agent. 23 Figure 6: PNNL VOLTTRON Architecture Diagram 6.1.8.3.1 Building / Device Controls 6.1.8.3.1.1 Water Heaters The project team developed and validated an affordable, interoperable, and user-friendly VOLTTRON water- heater (WH) control agent. This agent seamlessly manages CTA-2045 water heaters (via interfaces such as, e- Radio, SkyCentrics) and supports non-CTA-2045 WHs. It offers five CTA-2045 modes: Normal (default), Shed (moderate curtailment), Critical Shed (deeper curtailment), Load Up (pre-heat/absorb surplus), and Grid Emergency (maximum curtailment). The agent has been rigorously tested in laboratory settings using residential- sized WHs, both with and without the CTA-2045 control interface. Following a comprehensive review of the connected WH landscape, our project team was unable to find an affordable non-CTA-2045 controller for commercial-sized WHs. To confirm compatibility limitations, the team met with an A.O smith representative, who verified that the WH models in question do not support CTA-2045. Although retrofitting options were considered, the team ultimately decided against pursuing them due to feasibility concerns. As an alternative, the team explored leveraging the existing Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) network from existing meter installations. Discussions were held with Itron regarding the use of load control switch to manage the WHs via AMI. However, integrating the vendor’s proprietary distribution management intelligence software platform (Intellisource) with VOLTTRON proved to be a complex and non-trivial implementation. The team also investigated a solution from Eaton, given that Rocky Mountain Power (RMP) currently uses their Yukon platform for demand response purposes. A smart breaker was proposed but due to market limitations, specifically 24 the absence of a 90 A smart breaker posed a constraint. As a result, a custom solution is being explored, where a 90A contactor would have been connected to the WH disconnect switch which will then be controlled by the energy management smart breaker. The team subsequently evaluated an alternative approach utilizing Ace IoT solutions. This concept involves provisioning dedicated control panels for each bank of water heaters, totaling five panels. Each panel would be equipped with low-voltage temperature sensors, current monitoring sensors, and a gateway device integrated with VOLTTRON. Currently, this configuration appears to be the most feasible and cost-effective option. However, the team continues to assess additional strategies to identify the most scalable solution aligned with the project’s long-term objectives. This initiative is scheduled for the next budget period. 6.1.8.3.1.2 Air-Conditioners with Connected Thermostats The project team has identified two types of connected thermostats ideal for enhancing demand
